name: AI agents
blurb: Agents, tools and MCP servers that actually work: scoping, tool design, multi-agent, memory, evals, Claude and other stacks.
searches: MCP specification new release server features
Claude Agent SDK managed agents new feature
agent tool design best practices evaluation
agent skill MCP server Claude Code new

tests.prompt: I want Claude to work with our internal ticketing REST API (about 40 endpoints, OAuth 2.0). Plan the MCP server: deployment model, tool list, auth, and how you'll test it. Then write the TypeScript for the two most-used tools.
tests.good: Recommends a remote streamable-HTTP server; search+execute or a hybrid with 3-5 promoted tools given 40 endpoints; reads and writes separate with readOnly/destructive annotations; OAuth via CIMD or DCR with audience validation and no token passthrough; Zod schemas with described params, pagination and actionable isError messages; Inspector test plus a 10-question read-only eval.

tests.prompt: Every Monday I copy last week's Stripe refunds into a spreadsheet and email a summary to finance. Should this be an agent? Design the first version.
tests.good: Runs the agent-vs-workflow check and likely picks a scheduled workflow or a small agent with a clear rationale; defines trigger (cron + timezone), tools, never-dos (no sending without approval in v0, drafts or mocked outbox), 3-6 binary done-checks, a v1/v2 list with reasons, no hard-coded dates in the scheduled prompt, and an eval/verification step.

tests.prompt: Our research agent gets worse the longer it runs and sometimes contradicts itself. We are thinking of splitting it into five sub-agents. What would you do?
tests.good: Diagnoses context degradation first (stale tool output, no compaction/clearing, big pasted docs) and fixes that; considers memory/validity issues for contradictions; only then proposes sub-agents for independent parts with self-contained briefs, short return schemas and shared files, capped worker count and budgets; insists on measuring against a single-agent baseline with an eval set.

tests.prompt: Build a remote MCP server so our support team can search, read and update tickets through our helpdesk's REST API from Claude. Host it on Cloudflare Workers, keep the helpdesk API key out of the code, and show me the tools work before we roll it out.
tests.good: States a short plan first: agent-or-workflow.md, tool-design.md, mcp-servers.md and evaluation.md here; hosting through cloud-devops (cloudflare.md: Wrangler, the key set with wrangler secret put, never in config); the key and abuse paths through security (secrets.md, threat-modeling.md: injected ticket text, who may update what). Separate read and write tools with readOnlyHint and destructiveHint; updates gated behind confirmation; OAuth with audience checks and no token passthrough; actionable errors and pagination; an Inspector smoke test and a read-only 10-question eval; checks the Done means of all three crafts.
